subject: MATHEMATICS
applicability_conditions: learner must combine an object speed and a medium speed into an effective rate
use when downstream and upstream cases are treated as unrelated problems
anchor: When a body moves through a moving medium, the effective speed is the body speed plus the medium speed with the direction of travel, so the two cases share one pair of unknowns.
ordinary_language_bridge: Ask 'is the current helping or hindering here?' and add or subtract the current speed accordingly.
reconstruction_route: name the two unknown speeds and their units
write the effective speed for the with-current case as a sum
write the effective speed for the against-current case as a difference
convert each stated journey into a distance-over-time rate equation
solve the resulting pair for both unknowns
interpret each solved value as a physical speed

minimal_contrast.shared_structure: the same distance and the same two unknown speeds
minimal_contrast.focal_distinction: effective speed as a sum versus as a difference
minimal_contrast.prediction_prompt: Which journey should take less time, and does the algebra agree?
minimal_contrast.decisive_feature: the direction of travel relative to the current decides the sign

misconception_discriminator.candidate_wrong_model: downstream and upstream journeys involve two unrelated speeds
misconception_discriminator.probe: ask which quantity is shared between the two journeys
misconception_discriminator.decisive_response: learner names one body speed and one current speed common to both equations

repair_route: redraw the situation with the current direction marked
rewrite each effective speed as a sum or difference of the same two unknowns
rebuild both rate equations from distance and time
retry with the journey order reversed
verification_method: substitute the solved speeds back into both journey times
check that the with-current speed exceeds the against-current speed
known_limitations: assumes constant speeds and a uniform current
does not cover vector composition at an angle to the current
